---
title: DASCore 1.0
description: What is new in the DASCore 1.0 beta, and where to start.
---

We are excited to announce the DASCore 1.0 beta!

This release represents a huge amount of work. The [highlights](#highlights) below summarize the key features.

The beta is the time to try it on real data and tell us what breaks through the [issue tracker](https://github.com/DASDAE/dascore/issues) or the [discussions](https://github.com/DASDAE/dascore/discussions), before the API settles for 1.0. Your coding agent can do this with the [`dascore-test-beta` skill](https://github.com/DASDAE/dascore/blob/dev/dascore/.agents/skills/dascore-test-beta/SKILL.md); see [agent onboarding](../tutorial/agents.qmd).

Some changes break code written for 0.1.x. See the [migration guide](dascore_1.0_migration.qmd) for details.

## Install the beta

See [installing a pre-release](../installation.qmd#pre-releases); `[extras]` brings in the optional xarray and Parquet support used below. DASCore 1.0 also raises the minimum versions of Python, NumPy, and pandas; see its [`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/DASDAE/dascore/blob/dev/pyproject.toml).

## Highlights

- [A more flexible and efficient spool indexer based on SQLite](../tutorial/spool.qmd)
    - One [`Spool`](`dascore.Spool`) class; directory indexes support concurrent readers and writers, record every coordinate, and scale to millions of patches.
    - New methods: [`get_gaps`](`dascore.Spool.get_gaps`), [`get_coverage`](`dascore.Spool.get_coverage`), `unselect`, `load`, `cut`, `fill_gaps`, `snap_coords`, and `chunk(tolerance=...)`.
    - `chunk` joins patches whose seams are within `max_shift` and fits one grid per joined stretch. `tolerance` is now off by default; `tolerance=1.5` restores 0.1.x's joining.
- [The `Inventory`: a StationXML-inspired DAS metadata store](../tutorial/inventory.qmd)
- [The `AnnotationSet`: a data structure for managing annotations, including points and basic geometries](../tutorial/annotations.qmd)
- The [`PatchProcessor`](`dascore.PatchProcessor`): a structured class for separating metadata and data operations.
    - Chains of metadata can be processed without performing calculations
    - Kernels with non-NumPy backends (JAX, PyTorch) can be registered.
- [Coding agent skills and agent-friendly documentation, including a token-efficient CLI](../tutorial/agents.qmd)
- New Patch processors including:
    - [`window`](`dascore.Patch.window`) for efficiently applying ND windowed operations, and for moving-window reductions; it replaces `rolling`, which is deprecated.
    - multi-dimensional [`stft`](`dascore.Patch.stft`)/[`istft`](`dascore.Patch.istft`).
    - [`adaptive_spectral_filter`](`dascore.Patch.adaptive_spectral_filter`).
- [A re-imagined coordinate class to reduce rounding errors](../tutorial/coords.qmd)
    - Exact sampling grids keep fractional sampling rates through reading, writing, and merging.
    - Coordinates can hold gaps, handled by [`fill_gaps`](`dascore.Patch.fill_gaps`) and [`split_gaps`](`dascore.Patch.split_gaps`).
    - String coordinates are now supported.
- [Greatly improved compatibility with Xarray](../tutorial/xarray.qmd)
    - Generate xarray data trees from DASCore `Spools`
    - Access DASCore functions on the `dc` xarray namespace.
- [A simplified and more efficient FiberIO interface](../contributing/new_format.qmd)
    - Formats implement `get_version`, `get_metadata`, and `read_array`; [`dc.read_array`](`dascore.read_array`) reads part of a file without building a patch.
    - New readers: MiniSEED (v2 and v3), Sintela protobuf, AI4EPS, OptaSense ODH4, WITSML 1.4 DTS, Silixa H5 v2, and XDAS NetCDF. New writers: CF NetCDF-4 and Zarr.
- [Unique processing and patch identity markers](../notes/identity.qmd)
    - Lays a strong foundation for computational planning and data provenance tracking.
- [Support for remote files and directories thanks to universal-pathlib](../tutorial/remote_patches.qmd)
- [A new runtime configuration system, with process-wide defaults and thread-safe overrides](../tutorial/configuration.qmd)
- Support for free-threaded Python and Pyodide build targets (DASCore now runs in the browser!)
    - Tutorial pages open as live [marimo](https://marimo.io) notebooks in the browser with nothing to install.
- Improved representations including rich text and collapsible HTML representations for patches, spools, inventories, and annotation sets.
